report:
## Conclusion: The claim is well-supported by high-quality evidence.

Your conviction is justified. Multiple randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials and systematic reviews/meta-analyses confirm that add-on cannabidiol (CBD) reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome.

### Key Evidence

1. **Landmark Phase 3 RCT (GWPCARE1):** Published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* (2017), this trial randomized 120 children and young adults with Dravet syndrome to CBD (20 mg/kg/day) or placebo over 14 weeks. Convulsive seizures dropped from a median of 12.4 to 5.9 per month in the CBD group, a significant reduction compared to placebo. This provided Class I evidence. ([NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618))

2. **Dose-Ranging RCT (JAMA Neurology, 2020):** This trial found that adjunctive CBD at both 10 and 20 mg/kg/day produced "clinically relevant reductions in convulsive seizure frequency," with a better safety profile at the lower dose. ([JAMA Neurology](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458))

3. **Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis (CNS Drugs, 2020):** Lattanzi et al. pooled RCT data and confirmed CBD's efficacy as adjunctive treatment, with the main outcome being ≥50% reduction in baseline convulsive seizure frequency. ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32040850/); [Springer](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40263-020-00708-6))

4. **FDA Approval (2018):** The FDA approved Epidiolex (pharmaceutical-grade CBD) for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients ≥2 years old—the first-ever FDA-approved therapy for Dravet—based on the trial evidence above. ([FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210365lbl.pdf); [PMC review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7439947/))

### Caveats
CBD was associated with adverse events including somnolence, diarrhea, and elevated liver enzymes, and it is used as an **add-on** therapy, not a standalone treatment. Overall, the evidence is robust and consistent.
